self: I invest significant time in mentoring and developing my direct reports.
I prioritise team cohesion and consensus-building over individual speed.
I actively work to resolve interpersonal conflicts and preserve a supportive team environment.
I treat my team members with empathy and value them as members of the organisation.
I include everyone fairly and make sure all voices in my team are heard, regardless of role or background.
I recognise and celebrate team achievements, effort, and individual contributions.
I actively invest in the long-term career growth and well-being of each team member.
I seek input from my team before making decisions that materially affect them.
I make myself available to listen to both professional and personal concerns.
I build trust through consistent follow-through on the commitments I make to my team.
I encourage my team to take calculated risks, even when some attempts may fail.
I continuously scan the market for emerging trends, technologies, and customer needs.
I prefer flexible, non-linear approaches to solving complex business problems.
I thrive in ambiguity and can pivot quickly when conditions change.
I champion new product ideas, distribution models, and service innovations.
I challenge “the way we have always done it” thinking within my team.
I allocate time, budget, and resources for experimentation and pilots.
I articulate a compelling future vision for my function that energises the team.
I stay informed about new technology, digital transformation, and disruption in the sector.
I treat setbacks and failed experiments as opportunities to learn and iterate.
I define success primarily by meeting or exceeding KPIs, targets, and financial goals.
I push my team to outperform our competitors in the market.
I am comfortable being demanding to ensure deliverables are completed on time and to standard.
I stay close to customers and the market, tracking customer feedback, competitor moves and performance benchmarks.
I set stretch goals that raise the performance bar for my unit.
I hold my team rigorously accountable for results and the consequences of missed targets.
I make tough decisions quickly when performance is lagging.
I prioritise speed to market when launching new products, services, or campaigns.
I communicate a clear sense of urgency and competitive intensity in my team.
I translate wins into visible momentum that drives the next target.
I ensure every process in my area follows established SOPs and regulatory requirements.
I believe clear reporting lines, roles, and structure are essential to success.
I focus on technical accuracy and minimising errors in core operations, transactions, and client documentation.
I prefer predictable, proven outcomes over experimental approaches for core operations.
I track internal metrics, dashboards, and performance reports with discipline.
I document decisions, processes, and lessons learned for institutional memory.
I enforce adherence to internal controls, audit standards, and company policy.
I plan meticulously and manage resources within approved budgets.
I standardise workflows to ensure consistent service quality across teams.
I minimise operational risk through careful, methodical execution.
I conduct my work with transparency, honesty, and the highest ethical standards.
I ensure customers, clients or beneficiaries are treated fairly and receive services that genuinely meet their needs.
I consistently model the organisation’s core values in my decisions and behaviour.
I address unethical behaviour in my team promptly and firmly, regardless of performance record.
I safeguard confidential information and proactively manage conduct, compliance and reputational risk.
I communicate expectations, change, and strategic direction clearly to my team.
I actively invite challenge and dissenting views and respond without defensiveness or penalty.
I listen actively and demonstrate that I have understood the other party’s position before responding.
I give timely, specific, and constructive feedback, both positive and developmental.
I openly admit my own mistakes and treat others’ mistakes as opportunities to learn rather than to blame.
I align my team’s priorities with the organisation’s strategy and explain how each person’s work contributes to it.
I demonstrate a strong grasp of the organisation’s business or operating model: its key revenue or funding drivers, cost structure, and the metrics that matter most.
I anticipate how market, regulatory, economic, technological and social changes will affect the organisation.
I make data-informed decisions rather than relying solely on intuition or hierarchy.
I actively sponsor the adoption of digital tools and new ways of working in my team, rather than leaving it to the IT function.
I explain concretely what new behaviours, priorities and ways of working are expected during change.
I secure adequate time, budget and skilled people before launching major change.
I sustain momentum and follow through on change initiatives until results are visible.
I systematically apply lessons from past change efforts, both successes and failures, to new initiatives.
I balance short-term delivery pressure with long-term investment in people, capability and strategy.

open_self: What do you do as a leader that most helps your team succeed?
Where do you think your behaviour falls short of what your team needs from you?
Which of the four orientations do you rely on most under pressure, and what does that cost?
What feedback have you received in the last year that you have not yet acted on?
What would your team say you should start doing?
What one change in your leadership would make the biggest difference to the culture of your unit?

What should this leader stop doing?

Is there anything else that would help this leader develop?
